title: Prachinburi Nature Trip: 3 Days of Khao Yai, Waterfalls & Rafting | ThailandAddict
metaDesc: A 3-day, 2-night nature itinerary for Prachinburi, Thailand: the quiet Khao Yai entrance at Nern Hom, Haew Suwat, Haew Narok and Haew E-am waterfalls, plus whitewater rafting at Kaeng Hin Phoeng in Na Di — with times, entry fees and real rafting prices.
keywords: Prachinburi travel, Khao Yai Prachinburi side, Kaeng Hin Phoeng rafting, Haew Suwat waterfall, Haew E-am waterfall, Prachinburi nature itinerary
h1:
Prachinburi Nature Trip · 3 Days
Khao Yai Prachin Side · Waterfalls · Kaeng Hin Phoeng Rafting
intro: Most people know Khao Yai from the Pak Chong side, but Prachinburi has its own gateway into the park at Nern Hom — fewer crowds, denser forest, and the side that holds the biggest waterfalls, Haew Narok and Haew Suwat. Come back down toward Na Di district and you hit Kaeng Hin Phoeng, a whitewater run that only opens in the rainy season. This is a 3-day, 2-night plan that ties forest, waterfalls and fast water together without rushing.

blocks.html: This plan is written for people driving themselves, because Prachinburi's nature spots are scattered across the mountain and deep in the forest, well beyond what public transport can reach. There are three main zones: the Khao Yai Nern Hom side (Mueang district, heading up the mountain), the Prachantakham waterfall cluster like Haew E-am, Ta Khro and Than Thip, and Kaeng Hin Phoeng over in Na Di district. We put the mountain on day one, rafting on day two, and a slow waterfall stop on day three before heading home. Swap the order around to suit the rain.

blocks.title: Check before you set off
blocks.html: Kaeng Hin Phoeng rafting only runs in the rainy season, roughly June to October, because it depends on the runoff pouring down from Khao Yai. Outside that window the rapids are just a dry rock platform — no rafting. The big waterfalls like Haew E-am are also at their best in the rain. Plan a Prachinburi nature trip for the middle of the wet season and you get the full set.

blocks.text: Why the Prachinburi side of Khao Yai

blocks.html: Khao Yai has several entrances. The Pak Chong side (Nakhon Ratchasima) is busy and packed with cafés, while Prachinburi's Nern Hom gate is the quieter way up. You enter from Prachinburi town and climb steadily, passing the Nern Hom visitor centre to pay your entry fee, and the main ridge road then links you to the park's big waterfalls, both Haew Suwat and Haew Narok. The upside: shorter queues, thicker forest, and a real chance of spotting wildlife along the roadside like gaur or gibbons in the early morning.

items: Khao Yai entry fee — Thai adults 40 THB, children 20 THB; foreigners 200 THB adults, 100 THB children (paid at the Nern Hom gate). The ticket is valid all day.
Gate opening hours — opens early, around 06:00, and stops letting cars up the mountain in the late afternoon, so head up early to leave time for the waterfall walks.
Fuel up and pack everything before you go up — there are no petrol stations on the mountain and the mobile signal drops in and out.
It's cool up top and rain comes easily — always carry a rain jacket and shoes with decent grip.

blocks.label: Day 1
blocks.title: Up Khao Yai via Nern Hom — Haew Suwat & Haew Narok

items.activity: Leave Prachinburi town and head for the Nern Hom gate
items.note: If you're coming from Bangkok, drive in and spend the first night near town or at the foot of the mountain so you can get an easy early start.

items.activity: Reach the Nern Hom visitor centre, pay the park entry fee, then drive up
items.note: Mornings give the best odds of spotting animals by the road — drive slowly and never feed the wildlife.

items.activity: Haew Suwat waterfall — a single-tier drop about 20 m high, a short walk from the car park
items.note: It's the easiest Khao Yai waterfall to photograph; in the rainy season the water is powerful and the spray hangs in the air.

items.activity: Lunch break at the visitor area / park restaurant
items.note: Food options up the mountain are limited, so keep water and snacks in the car.

items.activity: Haew Narok waterfall — the tallest in Khao Yai, three tiers totalling over 150 m
items.note: A nature trail leads down to the viewpoint; it's fairly steep and slippery in the rain, so walk carefully.

items.activity: Head back down the mountain to your accommodation at the foothills / in town
items.note: Give yourself time to come down before dusk — visibility in evening mist and rain is poor.

items.activity: Dinner in Prachinburi town + rest
items.note: Tomorrow's rafting takes real energy, so turn in early.

blocks.label: Day 2
blocks.title: Rafting at Kaeng Hin Phoeng, Na Di — the real fast water

items.activity: Leave your accommodation and head to Na Di on the Kaeng Hin Phoeng side
items.note: From Prachinburi town to Na Di takes about an hour and a half, with the route passing villages and orchards.

items.activity: Arrive at the rafting base and pick a package with a local operator
items.note: A whole-boat charter (seats around 6) runs roughly 2,500–3,500 THB and usually includes life jackets, an on-board guide, insurance and park entry. Check what's included before you pay.

items.activity: Start rafting — about a 2.5 km run through 6 rapids in a row
items.note: It starts at Hin Phoeng rapid and runs through Phak Nam Lom, Wang Bon, Luk Suea and Wang Sai before finishing at Ngu Hao rapid — around 2 hours in total.

items.activity: Come ashore, change clothes, lunch by the water
items.note: Bring a spare set of clothes, a waterproof pouch for your phone, and strap-back sandals — you'll be soaked head to toe for sure.

items.activity: Swim in the stream / hang a hammock by the rapids, or wander the rock flats
items.note: In the rainy season the water is cold and fast — only swim where the staff allow it.

items.activity: Check in to your accommodation in the Kaeng Hin Phoeng / Na Di zone
items.note: There are both streamside resorts and campgrounds, from a few hundred to a couple thousand THB. Book ahead during the rainy high season.

items.activity: Riverside dinner, listening to the rapids
items.note: Many resorts have their own kitchen, so you can order dishes and eat right where you're staying.

blocks.label: Day 3
blocks.title: Prachantakham waterfalls — Haew E-am before heading home

items.activity: Breakfast at your accommodation, pack up
items.note: Today is an easy one — picking up a small waterfall along the way home.

items.activity: Move toward the Prachantakham waterfall cluster (Haew E-am / Ta Khro / Than Thip)
items.note: Take Highway 33, Prachantakham–Kabin Buri, then turn off at the Prachantakham junction following the waterfall signs.

items.activity: Haew E-am waterfall — a curtain of water about 25 m high deep in evergreen forest
items.note: It sits deep in the forest on the Prachinburi side and the walk in is fairly long. It's best in the rain, but if it's pouring or the trail is very slippery, gauge your own fitness first.

items.activity: Lunch in Prachantakham / Prachinburi town
items.note: Stop for boat noodles or local Prachinburi food before heading back.

items.activity: Pick up herbal souvenirs from Chao Phya Abhaibhubejhr before driving into Bangkok
items.note: Close out the nature trip with herbal products and a healthy-food spot in town.

items.activity: Drive home
items.note: Prachinburi to Bangkok is about 2–2.5 hours; avoid leaving at dusk to dodge the traffic on the way back.

blocks.text: Prachinburi-side Khao Yai waterfalls you shouldn't miss

items.name: Haew Suwat Waterfall
items.blurb: A single-tier drop about 20 m high, a short walk from the car park and easy to photograph — the perfect first waterfall of the trip.

items.name: Haew Narok Waterfall
items.blurb: The tallest in Khao Yai, three tiers totalling over 150 m, with a trail down to the viewpoint that's steep and slippery in the rain.

items.name: Haew E-am Waterfall
items.blurb: A curtain of water about 25 m high hidden in the evergreen forest on the Prachantakham side; the walk in is long, so it's for the adventurous only.

items.name: Pha Kluai Mai Waterfall
items.blurb: A mid-sized waterfall on the park's nature trail, good for an easy walk soaking up the forest atmosphere.

blocks.title: Safety things you need to know
blocks.html: Waterfalls and rapids are at their most beautiful in the rainy season, but that's also when the rocks are slipperiest and the water rises fastest. Always heed the staff announcements, never swim above the lip of a waterfall, and if it's raining hard upstream, get out of the stream immediately. Wear a life jacket the whole way down the rapids even if you can swim.

blocks.text: Kaeng Hin Phoeng rafting — know this before you book

blocks.html: Kaeng Hin Phoeng is in Na Di district — a wide rock platform at the start before you raft down the clear Yai stream, running through 6 rapids in a row over about 2.5 kilometres in roughly 2 hours. The intensity is fun for beginners who want the real thing without it being too brutal. The key point is that it only opens in the rainy season, since it relies on the runoff from Khao Yai — June to October is when the rafting is best.

items: Whole-boat charter price — around 2,500–3,500 THB per boat, seating about 6 people, usually including life jackets, a guide, insurance and park entry.
What to prepare — strap-back sandals or shoes that won't slip off, clothes you don't mind getting wet, a waterproof pouch for your phone, and a spare set to change into once you're ashore.
Valuables — leave them at the base or seal them tight in a waterproof bag, because the boat can flip on some rapids.
Book ahead — long weekends in the rainy season get busy, so contact a local operator or resort in advance.

items.name: Streamside stays in the Kaeng Hin Phoeng zone
items.blurb: Many resorts in Na Di sit right on the water, from a few hundred to a couple thousand THB, and some offer a rafting package so you can sort everything in one place.

items.name: Campgrounds by the rapids
items.blurb: For campers there are pitches under the trees near the stream with toilet facilities — great for falling asleep to the sound of the water, and easy on the budget.

blocks.text: Tips for planning a Prachinburi nature trip

items: The rainy season is the best value — you get both full waterfalls and rafting, but be ready for rain and slippery trails.
Driving yourself is by far the easiest — the three main zones are far apart and public transport doesn't reach them.
Spread your energy out — the mountain day and the rafting day both take a lot out of you, so don't pack both into one.
Carry cash — many forest service points and small resorts still only take cash.
Have a backup plan — if heavy rain cancels the rafting, switch to a small waterfall or the herbal spots in town instead.

faq.q: When is Kaeng Hin Phoeng rafting open?
faq.a: Only in the rainy season, roughly June to October, because it depends on the runoff from Khao Yai. Outside the rainy season the rapids are a dry rock platform and you can't raft. The middle of the wet season has the best water levels and is the most fun.

faq.q: How much does Kaeng Hin Phoeng rafting cost?
faq.a: A whole-boat charter runs about 2,500–3,500 THB per boat, seating around 6 people, and most include life jackets, an on-board guide, insurance and park entry. Check with the operator on exactly what's included before you pay.

faq.q: How do you enter the Prachinburi side of Khao Yai, and what's the fee?
faq.a: You enter via the Nern Hom gate in Mueang Prachinburi district and pay at the Nern Hom visitor centre: Thai adults 40 THB, children 20 THB; foreigners 200 THB adults, 100 THB children. Head up early to leave time for the waterfall walks.

faq.q: Do I need my own car for a Prachinburi nature trip?
faq.a: We recommend having your own car, because the main spots — Khao Yai's Nern Hom gate, the waterfalls and Kaeng Hin Phoeng — are scattered across the mountain and the forest, well beyond public transport. Without a car, the options are renting a car with a driver or buying a package from a local resort.

faq.q: Can this 3-day plan be cut down to 2 days?
faq.a: Yes. If you're short on time, drop the Prachantakham waterfall day: keep day one going up Khao Yai for Haew Suwat and Haew Narok, then day two rafting Kaeng Hin Phoeng before heading home. You'll still get the two main highlights in a short trip.
